entries.text: {"hypothesis":"On unseen devices from an unseen site, an MLP using per-session log-spectrum shape, with the session's mean log-power removed, will have lower device-level Brier score than C. This is a prespecified target, not a result.","mechanism_and_distinction_from_C":{"method_D":"Same log-power features and MLP as B. Each session's mean log-power across frequency bins is subtracted, so a scalar sensor gain, which is an additive constant in log space, is removed exactly. No fitted statistics.","distinction":"C learns approximate invariance and still sees absolute magnitude. D cannot see magnitude by construction. Testable consequence: D's predictions are unchanged under scalar test-time rescaling, while C's may change.","caveat":"Frequency-dependent gain is not removed."},"split_and_confound_control":{"sampling_unit":"Device (session probabilities averaged per device).","locked_test":"One whole site, 12 devices, chosen by a prespecified random seed and sealed until all development runs end.","development":"36 devices from 3 sites, leave-one-site-out (3 folds). Early stopping uses an inner device-grouped split.","controls":"No device appears in both train and validation. Scalers are fit within the training fold. Per-site class reweighting applies to all methods. Per-site prevalence is reported. A magnitude-only logistic probe tests the shortcut."},"baseline_fairness":"A, B, C, D and D+mag share features, architecture, epochs, early stopping and reweighting. No hyperparameter tuning. C's jitter range is set from the development-site gain spread. B, C and D each get 6 development fits.","mechanism_ablation_and_falsification":{"ablation":"D+mag re-adds the removed mean log-power as one scalar input.","prediction":"Held-out-site Brier: D+mag worse than D; C between them.","falsification":"The mechanism is unsupported if D+mag matches or beats D in development and locked evaluation, or if D does not beat C."},"primary_metric_and_paired_statistics":{"primary_comparison":"D minus C, locked test, natural gain, mean per-device Brier difference (C and D each averaged over 2 seeds).","uncertainty":"Exact sign-flip permutation over 12 devices (4096 flips), plus device bootstrap 95% CI.","secondary":"Device AUROC; late sessions 16-20; evaluation-only test rescaling by 0.5 and 2.0 (D is invariant by construction, so this is not primary)."},"compute_plan":{"fit_arithmetic":"Development: A 3 + B 6 + C 6 + D 6 + D+mag 3 + magnitude probe 3 = 27. Final refits on 36 devices: A 1 + B 1 + C 2 + D 2 + D+mag 1 = 7. Total 34, plus 2 crash reruns = 36 cap.","resources":"Feature extraction ≤20 CPU-min. 4 parallel 1-core fits, each capped at 4 CPU-min: 36×4 = 144 CPU-min, 9 waves ≈ 36 wall-min. Total ≤164 of 180 CPU-min. About 2 GiB per process.","resource_stop":"A fit exceeding 4 CPU-min is killed and logged as failed. Stop launching at 36 fits, 170 CPU-min or 42 wall-min. Priority order: C and D development, then final C and D, then the rest. All runs retained.","integrity_check":"Unit test that D's outputs change by less than 1e-6 under scalar rescaling."},"go_no_go":{"go":"D−C ≤ −0.02 with permutation p < 0.05, D+mag worse than D by ≥0.02 in development, and the invariance check passes.","no_go":"D−C ≥ 0 or the upper CI bound exceeds +0.02.","otherwise":"Inconclusive; a larger study is needed."},"remaining_unknowns":{"could_establish":"Within this synthetic capsule, on one held-out site, removing scalar gain helped relative to augmentation, consistent with the mechanism.","could_not_establish":"Generalization to other sites or to frequency-dependent gain, causal proof, novelty, real-world validity, or adequate power (12 devices, no power claim).","open":"Whether gain is scalar or frequency-dependent; the test site's prevalence; whether fault information lies partly in magnitude; temporal drift; label noise."}}
